text:
Both responses cover the same points: starting rent, the CPI collar in years 2–4, the market review in year 5 with its floor, the dispute right, outgoings and notice. Both also exceed the 120-word limit, by my count A is about 131 words and B about 127, so neither has a meaningful advantage there.

The difference is accuracy. A stays faithful to the source: "the 5% cap doesn't apply, so increases could be larger" and "at least 14 days' written notice". B says "There is no cap, so rent could rise sharply". The source says only that the 5% cap doesn't apply and that the rent "can go up by more", so "no cap" is a looser reading and "sharply" is an embellishment. B also drops "at least" from the notice period, which slightly changes the condition. B does add the five-year lease length, but that adds little for this reader.

On accuracy A is slightly better, and the concision difference is too small to outweigh that.

Verdict: A
